panels.figure_caption: Facial aspects and profiles of fetal SLOS in Case 3 at 23 weeks (a, d) Case 5 at 22 weeks (b, e), and Case 7 at 18 weeks (c, f). The male fetuses display prominent front with bitemporal narrowing, hypertelorism, short upturned nose, low set, dorsally rotated ears, long smooth philtrum, narrow lips, and microretrognathia. In Case 5, additional unilateral cleft lip and palate, and in Case 7 hydrops in the presence of bilateral renal agenesis were observed. SLOS, Smith‐Lemli‐Opitz syndrome
in_text_mentions: included intrauterine growth retardation (IUGR), brachymelia, and brachydactyly. Craniofacial dysmorphia comprised a prominent occiput and a flat face with bitemporal narrowing, hypertelorism, short flat upturned nose, long smooth philtrum, microretrognathia, and low set, dorsally rotated ears (Figure 1a–f). The severity score in Cases 3 to 5 ranged from >30 to 45, thus corresponding to a “more severe classical manifestation” of the disorder, whereas Case 7, presenting with bilateral renal agenesis and a severity score of 60, had to be classified as a “severe and lethal manifestation” of SLOS.

and Dandy‐Walker cyst (Figures 2, 3, 4). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Frontal clinical photograph of a patient with Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome displaying classic dysmorphic facial features associated with the disease, confirmed by the article's in-text clinical description. B: Lateral clinical photograph of the same patient with Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome, confirming the dysmorphic facial features consistent with the disease. C: Clinical photograph of the patient's foot demonstrating partial 2-3 toe syndactyly, a classic musculoskeletal manifestation of Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome. D: Dorsal clinical photograph of the patient's hand showing proximally placed thumb, a recognized hand abnormality in Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome confirmed by the article's in-text description. E: Palmar clinical photograph of the patient's hand demonstrating a single transverse palmar crease, a classic musculoskeletal manifestation of Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome.
